answer: The sonnet detector writes to voyage, and walnut makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 67 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 221 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
